title: Streamline continuous-batcher commit path and deprecate legacy scheduler lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Over time the continuous batching path accumulated ad-hoc commit semantics and write-throughs into the KV cache which increase tail latency and block the scheduler during GC/compaction windows. This ticket refactors the commit path, introduces an async persistence worker for eviction-safe snapshots, and removes legacy lane-level heuristics from the scheduler in favor of a compacted, event-driven fallback. Goals: (1) reduce 95th/99th token-generation latency during high-concurrency workloads by ~15-25%, (2) lower CPU contention on the scheduler thread, and (3) make KV eviction and snapshotting pluggable for future on-disk profiles.
comments: 2026-02-12 — Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem on high tail latency during the multi-tenant load test. Root cause: blocking commit path in continuous batcher while snapshotting KV slots.

2026-02-18 — Miguel Torres: Spike complete. Implemented prototype persistence worker that accepts epoched diffs and writes snapshots without blocking the main commit path. Microbenchmark shows commit critical path reduced by ~40% (p99 commit time). Link to spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CBP-17382-spike

2026-02-22 — Design review: Agreed to decouple persistence worker from eviction policy. Decided to keep in-memory commit acknowledgements synchronous for correctness but push durable writes off the hot path; this trades slightly longer time-to-durable for lower observed tail latency. Trade-off documented in design doc.

2026-02-26 — PR-branch: Opened GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8242. Early reviewers: @sliu, @jchen. Main changes: commit path fast-path, persistence worker, and metrics for commit-latency/persist-latency.

2026-03-02 — Perf run: Synthetic LLM workload (batch size distribution mirroring prod) shows token generation p95 down 18% and p99 down 12% versus baseline. CPU steady-state reduced ~9% across scheduler and batcher service processes.

2026-03-04 — QA: Found race where persistent snapshot applied concurrently with slot compaction caused transient consistency errors in rare long-conversation flows. Mitigation: add epoch fencing and retry window. Patch on PR to address fence ordering.

2026-03-08 — Scheduler cleanup decision: Remove legacy lane coalescing heuristics that attempted to balance lanes by size; replace with simple event-driven fallback that groups requests by latency target and model variant. This simplifies code path and reduces scheduler branch mispredictions in hotspots.

2026-03-11 — Security note from review: persistence worker writes only to customer-scoped ephemeral storage; production rollout must gate with KMS key-per-tenant. Added checklist item to rollout plan.

2026-03-12 — Miguel Torres: Addressed code-review feedback, added additional unit tests for epoch fencing and increased integration test coverage for heavy eviction scenarios. Preparing canary plan for runtime-1.20 canary ring. Next: coordinate Dedicated infra team for canary on reserved pools.
acceptance_criteria: Commit critical path latency (p99) must be reduced by >= 15% on the standard multi-tenant load test compared to master
No correctness regressions in long-conversation flows under compaction/eviction stress tested for 72h
Scheduler CPU utilization under representative workload reduced or unchanged; no >10% regression
Feature gated rollout plan exists that includes KMS gating, canary rings, and rollback instructions
Documentation updated: runtime docs + operator runbook updated with persistence worker config knobs
